moves.text: Someone must be standing Oren's watches when he doesn't show. Is it you?

made.text: Well now, that’s a sharp question. Why are you asking about Oren’s watches?
Well now, you’ve got a sharp eye. I have been covering some of Oren’s late watches—what’s got you asking?
Well, now you've put your finger on it. I've been covering some of Oren's late shifts; don't go making a song of it to the captain. Do you know why he's missing them?

moves.text: Who's been covering Oren's missed watches? The captain will notice sooner or later.

made.text: Well, that’s a sharp question. I’ve been taking the late watches myself; no need to make a public sport of Oren before we know what’s wrong with him.
Well, you do ask the awkward questions. I’ve been covering a few, but why are you asking about Oren?
Well, you’ve a sharp eye for a stranger. I’ve been covering a few of Oren’s watches—don’t go carrying that to the captain just yet. What makes you ask?
Well now, the sky’s doing its best to make a guard’s watch pleasant. You here for the gate, or just admiring the clouds?
Well now, the sky's doing its best to look harmless. What brings you up to the gate, Ash?
Well now, the sky's doing its part, at least. What brings you up to the gate, Ash?

moves.text: Where can I buy bread around here?

made.text: Well now, bread's at Hessa's inn, about thirty-eight steps down the road. She'll see you fed, and likely ask where you've been before the loaf's cut.
Well now, bread’s at the inn down the road—my sister Hessa runs the place. You after a loaf to take away, or a meal to sit down to?
Well now, bread’s at the inn door, about thirty-eight steps south. My sister Hessa runs the place; hard to miss unless you’re walking with your eyes shut.
Well now, Captain Roderic is at the gate, about five steps that way. What brings you looking for him?
Well now, that's Captain Roderic, at the gate. Are you looking to speak with him, or hoping to get through?
Well now, Captain Roderic is at the gate, about five steps that way. Looking to speak with him, or is there something you need from me?
Friend, I have linen, cordage, and a polished bronze mirror. Which sort of bargain are you after?
Friend, I’ve cloth, cordage, and a polished bronze mirror in the wagon. What catches your eye—and what have you to trade?
Friend, I’ve cloth, cordage, and a polished bronze mirror. Which catches your eye?

moves.text: Have you heard any news from the city?

made.text: A little, friend—but nothing I’d stake a bargain on. Have you heard anything worth carrying back the other way?
Not a scrap worth buying, friend. You hear anything that might turn a profit?
News travels at a price, friend, and I’ve no fresh word from the city worth selling. What have you heard?

moves.text: Oren can't pay you back. Would you let the debt go? It'd mean a lot to him.

made.text: Friend, Oren’s debt is no small sum to simply erase. What’s in it for me—and why should I trust you to make it worth my while?
Friend, I know Oren has a debt to me, and I don't write off coin on sentiment alone. Give me a good turn worth the sum, and we can square the account.
Friend, his empty purse is no reason for me to erase a debt. Give me a good turn worth the sum, and we can speak of squaring the account.

moves.text: You've got the compass now. Square it with me: let Oren's debt go.

made.text: A working compass is a handsome gift, friend. Oren’s debt is square; I’ll stop pressing him and keep the captain out of it.
Friend, that compass is a fine piece of value—and you did give it freely. Very well; Oren's account is squared. I won't press him or take it to the captain.
Friend, a working compass is a fine gift, but Oren's debt is another account. What would you put on the scales to make me write it off?

moves.text: That compass is yours to keep and copy. All I ask in return: let Oren off his debt.

made.text: Friend, that compass is already a handsome gift, but letting Oren's debt go is worth more than a novelty. What else can you put on the table?
A compass is a fine gift, friend, but Oren’s debt is another matter. What else might you put on the scales to make this bargain worth my while?
A compass, friend, is a handsome gift—but Oren's debt is good coin, and I don't erase it for a promise. What else is in this bargain for me?

moves.text: Boil the trough water before your guests drink it, like I showed you. Will you do that?

made.text: Aye, love. You showed me how it keeps folk well, and I’ll boil the trough water before it goes to the guests.
Aye, love. You showed me how, and I’ve seen it keep folk well. I’ll boil the trough water before the guests drink it.
I will, love. You showed me how, and I’ve seen it keeps folk well; I’ll boil the trough water before it reaches my guests.
Oh, love, a room is three coppers for the night. Need a bed for just yourself?
Oh, love, a room is two coppers for the night, supper not included. Shall I set one aside for you?
Oh, love, a room is three coppers for the night. Are you staying on your own?

moves.text: Is your brother on watch today?

made.text: Bren? He’s usually at the west post, love. I can’t say whether he’s on watch today, though.
He’s usually at the west post, love. Are you looking for him?
Oh, love, Bren usually keeps the west post at the gate. I couldn't say whether he's on watch today, though.

told.text: Tomas cracked the first beam himself, rushing the job.
Captain, your carpenter broke the old beam by hurrying it. That's why it's cracked.
Between us, Oren owes Darin eleven silver from dice.
Have you asked Tomas how the beam cracked?
I know something about Tomas, but it's not mine to tell.
Is Oren in some kind of trouble?
Good morning, captain. Any work going?
